messages:
carla_corp: Hey team, we're seeing 403 when trying to call the generation endpoint with the service key provisioned via our SSO. Embeddings calls succeed. Example curl we run:
```
  curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
    -H \"Authorization: Bearer sk_live_ABC...\" \
    -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" \
    -d '{"model":"redwood-mini","input":"hi"}'
```
Response: `403 Forbidden` and body: `{"error":"insufficient_permissions","message":"missing:generation"}`. Any quick ideas? This started after onboarding when we created an org service account via SSO.

jordan_support: Thanks Carla — sorry about the interruption. Can you confirm whether the key was created as a user key or an org/service key? Also can you paste the `GET /v1/keys/:key` output (obfuscated) or the UI view?

carla_corp: It's an org-level key created by our SSO provisioning. I can paste the UI screenshot but here's the JSON the console shows for scopes: `scopes: [\"embeddings\",\"rerank\"]` — no `generation`. I thought org keys should default to all inference scopes.

jordan_support: That explains the 403. SSO provisioning sometimes maps SCIM attributes to a subset of scopes. Two quick options: 1) ask your IdP admin to include the `redwood:allow_generation` claim in the SCIM/SAML mapping, or 2) we can grant the generation scope to the existing key on our side if you want us to.

sam_eng: Pinged — checking logs and the provisioning webhook. I see the initial provision call included `scopes=[embeddings, rerank]`. The provisioning lambda is defaulting to a minimal scope set unless `app_generation_allowed` claim is present in the token. Looks like your IdP didn't send it.

carla_corp: Ugh, ok. Is there a way to fix without rotating keys? We have infra that reads this key so rotation is tedious.

jordan_support: We can add generation to the existing key in the console (no rotation required) but we'll need an authorized request from an admin in your org. If you confirm, I can open an internal auth escalation to modify the key.

carla_corp: Confirmed — please add generation to key `sk_live_ABC...` (we'll message onboarding admin).

auth-bot: [audit] request received to modify scopes for key sk_live_ABC... by jordan_support. Approval required from Carla_Corp admin.

carla_corp: Approved. Admin (me) authorizes the change.

deploy-bot: rolling change: apply-scope-update sk_live_ABC... -> add [generation] (dry-run passed)

sam_eng: Done. I updated the key metadata — new scopes: `[embeddings, rerank, generation]`. Please retry your call.

carla_corp: Re-tested — generation now works, thanks! No client changes needed.

jordan_support: Great. Root cause: SSO/SCIM provisioning omitted the generation flag. Short-term fix applied (manual scope grant). Long-term: we should add a console warning when org keys created via SSO are scoped < full inference and add a docs page for common IdP mappings.

sam_eng: Filed ENG-1598 to add a validation step and a friendly banner in the UI. Also ENG-1599 to add a provisioning example for Okta/OneLogin showing the `redwood:allow_generation` claim.

jordan_support: Follow-up: Carla, we'll send a short KB explaining how to change mappings in Okta + the permission required for your SSO app. Also will include a checklist for future provisioning so teams don't miss generation.

carla_corp: Appreciate it. One small ask — can we get an audit log entry showing the timestamp of the scope change for our compliance team?

auth-bot: [audit] scope-change applied sk_live_ABC... +generation by sam_eng at 2029-06-11T15:28:19Z. Ticket: ENG-1598.

jordan_support: Sent the KB + compliance log to your email. Marking thread resolved, but keep us posted if anything else pops up. :thumbsup:
